summary: BREAK: reproduced a stale-cache incident. Injected bug removed cache invalidation from the DELETE path. Symptom: after deleting a link, GET /r/<code> still returned HTTP 302 with the old Location header (served from the Redis cache) instead of 404. Reproduced live via API: create -> redirect 302 (cache populated) -> delete 204 -> redirect again still 302 (stale).
evidence: create PJOkXV 2088 -> redirect 302 https://stale.example/z -> delete 204 -> redirect after delete 302 https://stale.example/z (expected 404, stale cache served)
root cause hypothesis: DELETE write path omits invalidate_redirect_target, so the cached code->url entry survives the row deletion and outlives it until TTL
confirmed by inspecting links.py delete_link handler: no cache invalidation call
